post-body:
Quick answer

Over a decade, hardwood asks less of you — and of your wallet — than carpet. Carpet needs weekly vacuuming, a professional deep clean every 12–18 months, restretching when ripples appear, and full replacement every 8–15 years. Hardwood needs weekly dusting, an occasional damp mop, and a $1.99/sq ft buff and recoat every 3–5 years — it gets refinished, never replaced. Full disclosure: we're OC Flooring, a hard-surface company — we don't sell or install carpet, so no carpet commission is riding on this comparison.

Marysville & Snohomish County 10-year math below (425) 595-1079

Most carpet-versus-hardwood arguments happen at the install quote, where carpet wins easily. The honest comparison happens over the next ten years of Saturdays — who's vacuuming what, who's paying the steam-cleaning truck, and which floor needs replacing while the other gets a refresh. We've installed and refinished hardwood across King and Snohomish County since 2013, and we've pulled a lot of tired carpet out of Marysville family homes along the way. Here's the upkeep scorecard we'd give a friend, with the same honesty we bring to every free in-home estimate.

The Upkeep Gap in Three Numbers

12–18 mo

the professional deep-clean interval carpet makers recommend — and many warranties quietly require. Figure $120–$240 a visit at 2026 market rates.

8–15 yrs

the realistic carpet replacement cycle in a busy family home. Hardwood doesn't have a replacement cycle — it has a refinishing cycle.

$1.99/sq ft

our buff-and-recoat price: the every-3-to-5-years reset that keeps a hardwood finish from ever wearing through to bare wood.

The Weekly Routine, Side by Side

Carpet, weekly

  • Vacuum once or twice — slow passes, extra attention to traffic lanes
  • Blot spills immediately, before they wick into the pad below
  • Spot-treat pet accidents the hour they happen, not that weekend
  • Shake out doormats — grit is what shears carpet fiber

Hardwood, weekly

  • Sweep or dust-mop the main paths
  • Vacuum on the hard-floor setting (beater bar off)
  • Damp — never wet — mop with a wood-floor cleaner as needed
  • Wipe spills whenever you happen to find them

Week to week, the effort is nearly a tie — both floors mostly want a vacuum. The difference is what happens when life happens. A spilled glass of juice sits on hardwood until someone wipes it; it sinks into carpet and becomes a project. Our full hardwood routine, product names included, is in how to clean and maintain hardwood floors.

The Annual Calendar Each Floor Expects

Carpet's year is built around the deep clean: hot-water extraction every 12–18 months at $120–$240 per visit market rate — sooner with kids and pets — plus re-applying stain protection afterward, and a restretch (roughly $120–$350 for a whole home at market rates) whenever ripples or wrinkles appear. Skip the deep cleans and two things happen: the carpet ages visibly faster, and many manufacturer warranties lapse for lack of receipts.

Hardwood's year is almost embarrassingly short: fresh felt pads under the furniture, pet nails trimmed, and an eye on winter humidity — heating season dries our indoor air, and boards are happiest between about 35 and 55 percent. The only recurring professional visit is a buff and recoat every three to five years, which adds a fresh wear layer before the old one wears through. The rest of the playbook fits in one read: five ways to protect hardwood flooring.

The 10-Year Cost of Ownership

Install prices get all the attention, so let's hold them aside and compare only what each floor costs to own. The asymmetry is the whole story: money spent on carpet slows its decline, while money spent on hardwood actually resets it. At year ten the recoated hardwood looks new; the deep-cleaned carpet is shopping for its successor.

Over 10 years (per 1,000 sq ft)Mid-grade carpetSite-finished hardwood
Professional cleaning$1,200–$2,400 (8–10 deep cleans)$0 — routine cleaning is DIY
Restretching / small repairs$150–$400$100–$400 (odd board or scratch)
Scheduled resetNone available — wear is permanent1–2 buff & recoats: $2,000–$4,000
Replacement within the decade$3,500–$7,000 once by year 8–15$0 — a $3.99/sq ft refinish replaces replacement
10-year upkeep total$4,850–$9,800$2,100–$4,400

*Carpet figures are 2026 market rates for comparison — not our quotes; we don't sell carpet. Buff-and-recoat ($1.99/sq ft) and refinish ($3.99/sq ft) figures are our actual prices.

The same logic is why our refinishing service exists at all: a hardwood floor that looks finished is usually one $3.99/sq ft sanding away from looking installed-yesterday — no tear-out, no new material, no landfill run.

Pets, Kids, Allergies, and Wet Novembers

The spreadsheet rarely decides this question alone. Four household realities usually do:

  • Allergies. Hard floors don't store dander, dust, or pollen — what lands on them leaves with the next sweep. The old claim that carpet "filters" allergens only holds if it's deep-cleaned religiously; in practice, most allergists and most noses side with hard surfaces.
  • Pets. An accident on carpet wicks into the pad and returns as odor on humid days. On hardwood it's a paper towel — and even a stain that soaks a board is fixable: we handle exactly that kind of hardwood floor repair in Marysville routinely. Claw scratches sand out at the next recoat; carpet snags don't un-snag.
  • Kids. Carpet forgives tumbles and muffles a two-story house. The have-it-both-ways answer is hardwood with a washable area rug — softness where you want it, and the rug goes in the laundry.
  • Our climate. From November to March, everything entering a Marysville house is wet. Entry carpet absorbs that and stays damp; hardwood wipes dry in seconds.

Lifespan: Replacement Cycle vs. Refinishing Cycle

Carpet tells you when it's done: matting the vacuum can't lift, permanent traffic lanes, ripples that return after a restretch, odors that survive a deep clean. In a busy household that day arrives in 8–15 years — sooner in halls and stairs. Our guide to how often flooring should be replaced covers the signs floor by floor. And if carpet is the right call for your bedrooms, buy it well: our unbiased carpet brand roundup exists precisely because we have nothing to sell in that aisle.

Hardwood works on a different clock entirely. A 3/4-inch solid floor can be sanded and refinished several times over a 50-to-100-year life, and most of the "ruined" floors we're shown — gray traffic paths, water marks, pet stains — are one refinish from looking new. That's the difference between a floor you replace and a floor you maintain.

What Upkeep Means for Resale in Marysville

Marysville's housing stock is young by Puget Sound standards — heavily 1990s and 2000s planned subdivisions, overwhelmingly single-family, and bought by families. Which means a large share of the city's original builder-grade carpet is now 20 to 30 years old, well past its design life, and buyers can tell the moment the door opens. In a market that has appreciated as fast as Marysville's, worn carpet gets read as a to-do list — and mentally deducted at more than its replacement cost — while fresh hard surfaces on the main floor read as move-in ready.

The pattern that keeps winning in family neighborhoods: hard surfaces on the main level where traffic, pets, and wet boots live, carpet upstairs where bare feet and quiet matter. And if your home already has hardwood hiding under that aging carpet — common even in 1990s builds — refinishing it before listing is one of the highest-return moves a Marysville seller can make: refinish cost is a fraction of what buyers will pay for "gorgeous hardwoods" in the listing photos.

When Carpet Wins, When Hardwood Wins

Carpet wins…

  • Bedrooms, where warmth underfoot beats everything at 6 a.m.
  • Upstairs halls and media rooms, for sound-deadening
  • Playrooms, where soft landings matter
  • The install quote — lowest day-one cost, every time

Hardwood wins…

  • Main floors, kitchens-adjacent spaces, and entries
  • Allergy households and pet households
  • The 10-year math — upkeep that resets instead of slows decline
  • Resale day, in Marysville and everywhere else

If you run that split — hard surface down, carpet up — get each floor from people who specialize in it. Bundled whole-house deals usually price one half poorly, and it's rarely the carpet half.

Carpet vs. Hardwood Upkeep Questions, Answered

Is hardwood or carpet easier to maintain?
Week to week they're similar — both mainly need vacuuming. Over years, hardwood is easier and cheaper: no professional cleanings, no restretching, and no replacement cycle. A recoat every 3–5 years resets the finish, and a full refinish renews the floor for decades.
How often should carpet be professionally cleaned?
Every 12–18 months, at roughly $120–$240 per visit at 2026 market rates — more often with kids and pets. Many carpet warranties require proof of professional cleaning on that schedule, so keep the receipts.
How often do hardwood floors need refinishing?
A buff and recoat every 3–5 years keeps the finish healthy, and a full sand-and-refinish is typically needed every 10–20 years depending on traffic. A solid hardwood floor survives several refinishes over a 50-to-100-year life.
Which is better for allergies, carpet or hardwood?
Hard surfaces, for most households. Hardwood doesn't store dander, dust, or pollen — it leaves with the next sweep. Carpet can trap allergens out of the air, but only deep, frequent cleaning actually removes them from the home.
How long does carpet last compared to hardwood?
Mid-grade carpet realistically lasts 8–15 years in a family home, less in halls and stairs. Solid hardwood lasts 50–100 years because it gets refinished instead of replaced — the surface renews while the floor stays.
Does replacing carpet with hardwood help resale in Marysville?
Generally, yes. Marysville's family-oriented market reads worn carpet as a project and fresh hard surfaces as move-in ready. Refinishing existing hardwood before listing is usually the highest-return version of the move.
Does OC Flooring install carpet?
No — we're a hard-surface company: hardwood installation and refinishing, vinyl plank, and laminate across King and Snohomish County. That's why the carpet figures in this guide are unbiased market rates; we have no carpet to sell you.
